What has the community built on top of LTX that stood out for you?
Okay, so the cool thing to see with what people are building is sometimes really unexpected ideas.
We started our journey of creating foundational models from the perspective of creative tools.
We had LTX Studio that initially was built on top of our models and then we realized that we need to have our models in order to keep evolving it.

What stands out are the things that you couldn't predict before and are completely new for us.
And they're also completely outside of the domain of what we're doing.
We started our journey with LTX in order to create a super efficient model that can run on edge devices and can power our own products.
And now we're seeing, for example, people who are using LTX for robotics.
They have specialized data sets, for example, of what robots are doing in warehouses or how humans are manipulating objects in the manufacturing pipelines, etc.
And they start to fine-tune the model with this data and repurpose it for robotics use cases.
We start to see people who are using it for agriculture and drones, etc.
Things are really, really far away from what we're doing.
Another kind of cool thing are people who are trying to bring LTX to complete real-time low-latency models.
And they start to build avatars.
And they started to think how they can create programmatic content with it.
I think it validates our intuition that diffusion models are this magical piece of tech.

We're going to see completely new things.
We already see it with LTX.
